title: Vector Components
body:
Resolving a [[Vector]] into **components** replaces one vector at an angle with two vectors
along the axes, which turns a two-dimensional problem into two one-dimensional problems.

```
magnitude 20 at 30° above the horizontal

  vₓ = 20 cos 30° = 17.32
  v_y = 20 sin 30° = 10.00

back the other way:  |v| = √(vₓ² + v_y²),   θ = arctan(v_y / vₓ)
```

Cosine goes with the angle's adjacent axis and sine with the opposite one, so which function
belongs to which component depends on where the angle is measured from. Drawing the triangle
before writing the formula is what prevents the standard error.

The components are independent, which is the fact the whole two-dimensional half of the course
uses. In [[Projectile Motion]] gravity changes the vertical component and leaves the
horizontal one alone, so the two are solved separately and combined at the end.
